content.title: Samsung’s New Deadline—You Have 12 Weeks To ‘Upgrade’ Your Phone
content.text: Dop not miss this deadlineFuture Publishing via Getty ImagesIt has finally happened — Samsung is killing another of its own apps to go all in with a Google stock offering. The Galaxy-maker warns that users have until July to make changes on their phones before this big new switch-off.We’re talking Samsung Messages, Galaxy’s secure messaging alternative to the Google Messages app that has become the default across Android. “The Samsung Messages application will be discontinued in July 2026,” the company confirmed Saturday. “Upgrade to Google Messages as your default messaging app today.”ForbesFBI Warns iPhone And Android Users—Do Not Install These AppsIt’s unclear how many Galaxy users still use Samsung Messages over Google’s alternative. It’s also unclear how much this matters, given WhatsApp’s dominance across Android. While RCS has enabled secure Android messaging as an alternative to WhatsApp, this has required all ends of a conversation to use the same app, thus the push to Google Messages. But whatever the stats may be, it’s the end of an era.“Check the Samsung Messages app for the exact date when service will be discontinued,” Samsung says, pointing out that “older Android OS (Android 11 or lower) are not affected by this End of Service,” and that “the Google Messages icon will not automatically shift into the home screen” on Android 12 and 13.How to 'upgrade' your phone.SamsungOnce the deadline hits, you won’t be able to send any messages via Samsung’s app, “except for emergency service numbers or emergency contacts." And users are warned that on pre-2022 Galaxy phones “switching messaging applications may temporarily disrupt ongoing RCS conversations.” Google Messages is intended to be Android’s alternative to Apple’s iMessage, which retains strong market share in the U.S., despite the global dominance that WhatsApp has now secured, with 3 billion users and counting. But Android’s stock messenger is let down by the lack of cross-platform, secure messaging or the same kinds of OS hooks that Apple has built into its own platform.ForbesIf You See This Message In Google Chrome, You Are Now At RiskBy Zak DoffmanFor Samsung and its billions of users, this is another example of Google’s increasing control of the full Android OS, which now includes its AI take-over with Gemini, relegating Samsung’s Bixby and other other offerings to also-rans. The AI space race and Samsung’s positioning versus Apple is a much bigger issue for Samsung than messaging, as is increasingly being pointed out.
